solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Inaccurate stroke perfected by repetition (3,3)

blocks.note: off = inaccurate, as in 'my guess was off'

annotation.surface: A sports coach grumbles about a wayward shot that was drilled until it came right.
annotation.walkthrough: Something known off pat has been learnt by rote, so 'perfected by repetition' is the definition while the first two words build it.
annotation.definitionFit: Knowing something off pat means having it word-perfect from repetition.

entries.clue: Draw line between Florence and those surrounding settlements (5)

indicatorNotes.those surrounding: the letters that surround 'settlements' are its outer ones, S and S

blocks.note: Flo is the short form of the name Florence
first and last letters of settlements

annotation.surface: A town planner draws a boundary between Florence and the villages round it.
annotation.walkthrough: The map-drawing surface hides the dentist: to floss is to draw a thread between the teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: Flossing means drawing a line of thread between your teeth.

entries.clue: Republicans’ preferred leader now concealing identity (9)

indicatorNotes.concealing: PRESENT conceals ID, holding it inside

blocks.note: ID = identity, as in an ID card

annotation.surface: A party's favourite for the top job is keeping who they really are under wraps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Republicans' is not the US party but anyone who wants a republic: they prefer a president as head of state to a monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Republics are led by presidents rather than kings, so a president is what republicans want at the top.

entries.clue: Very friendly con swapping sides for rematch (5)

indicatorNotes.swapping: one letter is swapped for another
indicatorNotes.sides: the sides of 'rematch' are its outer letters, R and H

blocks.note: rematch's sides are R and H; R in TRICK is swapped for H

annotation.surface: A cheat, beaten once, changes teams in order to get another game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swapping sides' sounds like changing teams; here it means swap one side letter of 'rematch' (R) for the other (H), turning TRICK into THICK.
annotation.definitionFit: People who are thick are very close friends, as in 'thick as thieves'.

entries.clue: Constant husband charged with fling remains grumpy (8)

indicatorNotes.charged with: C and H are charged, or loaded, with the other pieces, which go between them

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
remains = is, as in 'the problem remains' / 'the problem is'

annotation.surface: A husband caught out in an affair stays loyal but goes on sulking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constant husband' reads as a faithful spouse, but it is two abbreviations, C and H, that open and close the answer with the rest loaded between.
annotation.definitionFit: Churlish means surly and bad-tempered, which is grumpy.

entries.clue: Honesty positively helpful with jury, getting case dismissed (7)

indicatorNotes.getting case dismissed: the case of 'jury' is its outer letters, J and Y, which are dropped

blocks.note: can-do, as in a can-do attitude

annotation.surface: A witness is frank and cooperative with the jury, and the case against someone is thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom words are all misdirection: 'case dismissed' is not a verdict but the shell of JURY being stripped off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: candour is the frank, open quality of saying what you think.

entries.clue: Take cover from sun’s heat, heeding limits (9)

indicatorNotes.limits: the words before it limit, or enclose, the answer

blocks.note: the run starts at the second letter of sun's and stops after the HE of heeding

annotation.surface: Advice to shelter from the midday sun while respecting safe limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take cover from' looks like 'shelter from'; read it as 'take the cover off', which is what unsheathing a sword does.
annotation.definitionFit: Read literally: the sheath is a blade's cover, so taking that cover off is unsheathing.

entries.clue: Litre per person let out through porous material (5)

blocks.note: five pounds each = five pounds per person

annotation.surface: A ration of a litre a head is doled out through a filter.
annotation.walkthrough: Chemicals leach out of soil when water drains through it, carrying them away.
annotation.definitionFit: To leach is to drain or seep out through something porous such as soil.

entries.clue: When upset go to bed, heading off extremely gloomy (9)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down, so AS reads SA
indicatorNotes.heading off: the heading of 'extremely' comes off it: its first letter

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: A sulker's advice: when you are upset, just go to bed, and you are terribly glum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like it qualifies 'gloomy'; it is only there to lend its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, supposedly born under Saturn.

entries.clue: Drifting mid-ocean, might one benefit from good routine? (8)

annotation.definition: might one benefit from good routine?

indicatorNotes.Drifting: the letters drift out of place

annotation.surface: Someone adrift at sea might do well from a sensible daily regimen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Routine' means a daily habit in the surface but a comic's set of jokes in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A comedian's act is called a routine, and a good one is what they profit from.

entries.clue: Ramshackle home will not last for tenancy (6)

annotation.surface: A tumbledown house won't stay standing for the length of the lease.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Will not last' reads as a single phrase, but it splits: 'will not' is SHAN'T and 'last' points at the end of 'tenancy'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shanty is a crude hut knocked together from scrap, the ramshackle home the surface describes.

entries.clue: Censure own goal during tie to remain in league (5,8)

indicatorNotes.during: OG comes during TETHER, inside it

blocks.note: to give someone stick = to censure them
OG = own goal in football reports

annotation.surface: Pundits slam a team whose own goal in a cup tie keeps them in the league.
annotation.walkthrough: The football words are all misdirection: 'league' means alliance, and 'tie' is a rope, not a match.
annotation.definitionFit: People who stick together stay allied, in league with each other.

entries.clue: Cycling round Lewis, see western one? (4)

indicatorNotes.Cycling round: letters are moved from the front of the word round to the back

blocks.note: LEWIS with LE cycled round to the end
W, the western letter, is dropped

annotation.surface: A cyclist riding round the island of Lewis sees another of its neighbours.
annotation.walkthrough: Lewis is one of the Western Isles off Scotland, so a 'western one' is an isle; the clue is loose and leans on that ?.
annotation.definitionFit: Lewis belongs to the Western Isles, so one of them is an isle.

entries.clue: Eg “One giant leap”, its location given by Spooner? (9)

indicatorNotes.given by Spooner: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: swap the B and S sounds

annotation.surface: Armstrong's famous moon-landing line, and where it was spoken, as the Reverend Spooner might put it.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation does double duty: it is an example of a sound bite, and 'giant leap' is also a BOUND.
annotation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong's 'one giant leap for mankind' is a classic short, quotable sound bite.

entries.clue: Processing unit collects university fees, assisting ministry (10)

indicatorNotes.collects: CHIP collects U and RATES, taking them inside

blocks.note: a microchip is a computer's processing unit

annotation.surface: A computer centre takes in university fees to help a government department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ministry' suggests government; here it is the church's ministry, and a curate assists the vicar.
annotation.definitionFit: A curateship is the post of curate, a priest who assists in a parish ministry.

entries.clue: Note supplier from China struggling with post (9)

indicatorNotes.struggling: the letters struggle out of order

annotation.surface: A letter-writer's supplier in China is having trouble with the postal service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'post' suggest letters; the notes are banknotes. A cashpoint is the British name for a cash machine or ATM.
annotation.definitionFit: A cashpoint, or ATM, supplies banknotes.

entries.clue: Trace family’s heir with input from American detective (9)

indicatorNotes.with input from: US and PI are put into SCION

blocks.note: a scion is an heir or descendant of a family

annotation.surface: A genealogist tracks down a family's heir with the help of an American private eye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trace' looks like a verb, as in tracing a family; it is the noun, a tiny amount, as in 'a suspicion of garlic'.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: a suspicion can mean a faint hint, as in 'a suspicion of a smile'.

entries.clue: Embarrassed at poem, thus squirming (3,2,5)

indicatorNotes.squirming: the letters squirm into a new order

annotation.surface: A poet squirms with embarrassment at their own verse.
annotation.walkthrough: The squirming belongs to the letters as well as the embarrassed reader, so the surface acts out the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom in the past tense: shown up by someone better, you feel humbled and your cheeks burn.

entries.clue: Trouble squeezing letters in for marginal note (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' completes 'squeezing ... in': the letters are squeezed in, inside the trouble

blocks.note: to ail = to trouble, as in 'what ails you?'

annotation.surface: An editor struggles to fit extra letters into a note in the margin.
annotation.walkthrough: An apostil (or apostille) is an old word for a note in the margin of a book.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare word: an apostil, also spelt apostille, is an annotation written in a page's margin.

entries.clue: Cook makes moist rolls (4)

annotation.surface: A cook glazes bread rolls to keep them soft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' pretends to be bread; it is the instruction to turn WETS round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a verb: to stew food is one way to cook it, simmering it slowly.

entries.clue: Trench mortar on day one not going off as hoped (13)

indicatorNotes.on: SAP and POINTING come on, after, D and I

blocks.note: a sap is a military trench dug towards the enemy
pointing is the mortar between bricks

annotation.surface: A First World War shell fired on the opening day is a dud.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trench mortar' is a real weapon, which is why the phrase holds together so well; it has to be split into two words. 'Going off' fits both a shell and an event.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a let-down event is one that did not go off as hoped.

entries.clue: Can it imitate fashion? (5)

annotation.surface: A question whether it is possible to copy what is in vogue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' as a noun fits the surface; as a verb it means to shape something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to fashion a pot or a plan is to give it form.

entries.clue: Bottle still spinning overcomes resistance (5)

indicatorNotes.spinning: something spinning turns round, so EVEN is read the other way, NEVE
indicatorNotes.overcomes: in a down clue, NEVE comes over R, holding it

annotation.surface: A spinning distillery vat wears down the opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so it means nerve; 'still' is not a distillery but EVEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, which is nerve.

entries.clue: Shower beneath grand timber structure (5)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, RAIN goes beneath G

annotation.surface: Rain drips down under a large wooden shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Timber structure' suggests a building; it is the pattern of fibres in wood.
annotation.definitionFit: The grain of wood is the arrangement of its fibres, its structure.

entries.clue: Festival key in India, taking short week (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: DIAL takes W in, the way a house takes in a lodger

blocks.note: to key in a number = to dial it
India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A major festival in India lasts less than a full week.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key in India' reads as 'central to India', but 'key in' is a phrasal verb meaning dial; the festival of lights really is in India.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, one festival among many.

entries.clue: Last minute cuts restored later (8)

indicatorNotes.cuts: MIN cuts into the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.restored: LATER is re-stored into a new order

annotation.surface: Budget cuts made at the eleventh hour were reversed afterwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last minute' reads as one phrase, but 'Last' is the definition and 'minute' is MIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Terminal means final, last, as in a terminal stage.

entries.clue: Column left behind regrouped at speed (8)

indicatorNotes.behind: 'left behind' puts L behind, at the end of, the regrouped letters
indicatorNotes.regrouped: AT SPEED is regrouped into a new order

annotation.surface: A marching column's straggler catches up after the troops re-form at a run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Column' is an army formation in the surface and a pillar in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a pillar-like base, a short column supporting a statue.

entries.clue: A little variation in level reflected warming at sea (2,4)

indicatorNotes.A little: a little of the next words, a run of letters inside them
indicatorNotes.reflected: the run reads backwards, as in a mirror

annotation.surface: A small change in sea level shows up because of warmer ocean temperatures.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is real oceanography, so it is easy to look for a word for 'rise' rather than a hidden reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: El Niño is the periodic warming of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
